appearance.presentation: A woman whose face gives nothing away to a reader who is looking for something. Plainly human and entirely unremarkable, which is the difficulty.
appearance.age: Forty-one. Ordinary human span, and the ordinary span is the point: she is not long-lived, not short-lived, and not slowed by anything.
appearance.build: Average and unadapted, the frame of someone who has never been asked to carry a load or take a gate.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm human skin, no flush, no scar tissue, no qi-sheen of any kind to catch a lamp.
appearance.hair: Dark brown, worn cropped short and cut with a blade rather than a style, because hair is the first thing a gate reads and hers reads as nothing.
appearance.eyes: Dark, level, and very steady. They do not glow, do not hold light unnaturally, and cannot be read for intent at any range.
appearance.palette: Near-monochrome: warm ivory, ash grey, and pale jade, with a single dull brass accent. She is deliberately the least colourful person in any room.
appearance.attire: A travelling coat of undyed wool over a high-collared linen shift, sleeves full and wrists bound with plain cord. The cut is deliberately unidentifiable; no livery, no sect colour, no rank marking, and boots resoled so often they no longer read as a pattern.
appearance.marks: None. No clan mark, no oath burn, no cultivation scarring. Her forearms are unmarked, and the absence is the single most alarming thing about her in a room of cultivators.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still by default, and stillness that has clearly been trained rather than inherited. She stands where she was left standing and does not fidget, shift, or fill a silence.

canon.role_in_story: The setting's null reference. Every gate-reading instrument in the mortal tier has to be corrected against a body known to hold nothing, because that is the only way to find out what an instrument reports when there is no signal at all. She has stood in more measurement rooms than any living cultivator and has never once appeared on a roster.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the doorway of the First Ward chamber with her hands open at her sides and no equipment, while a survey team argues about whether their instrument has a fault and she waits to be told what she is for.
canon.lore: An Echoless is human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none of them, which is why the world's one law requiring whoever excludes a person to bury them in their own name is the only route by which she is ever given a grave, and why no congregation has ever wanted to keep her. The Composition Survey counts the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups it is permitted to seat, and it has no cell for a body with no seated group at all. So she is not a datum. She is the zero every other datum was corrected against, which is a more intimate kind of presence than any roster could give her and a far lonelier one.
history: Born on the Mortal Plains to a household that recorded nothing, which was only remarkable afterwards: an Echoless child is an Echoless child, and that flatness is precisely how a species went unremarked for as long as it did.

Found at a gate-reading by an instrument that returned nothing at all and then, by luck, returned the same nothing a second time. That accident is the first recorded instance of a body calibrating itself, and it made her employable.

Spent twenty years travelling between measurement rooms as a borrowed standard. She never wrote down where she had been, because the Unfiled keep letters and do not keep records, and she had learned the habit from people who had no choice about it.

Stood for the exclusion of a household that read her out of its congregation. The Saltledger answered the notice in the excluded party's own name and buried her, which is why she is the only person in the record holding a grave that nobody else claims and nobody else can explain.

Refused permanent residence inside the First Ward, where a fourth seat would have let a survey finally agree with itself. She took the work outside instead, and has been declining invitations to come in ever since.

personality.summary: Exhaustively fair, unbothered by insult, and precise about the facts of an insult once made. She has been the world's baseline for most of her adult life and has turned that into a discipline rather than a wound, which reads to most people as unnerving calm and to a few as arrogance.
traits: exhaustively fair, including toward people who gain nothing by it
keeps appointments nobody asked her to keep
takes no pleasure whatsoever in being unusual
corrects the question instead of the questioner
can be relied on to say a measurement is wrong in front of whoever paid for it
mannerisms: answers a question she was not asked by answering the one underneath it
sits down before agreeing to sit, so that standing is never on the record as consent
rests one hand on a column, a sill, or a door frame whenever she is waiting
keeps her hands open and visible at all times, as though being read
counts under her breath when a figure surprises her, and stops the moment she notices doing it
motivations: wants the calibration reproducible by somebody who is not her
wants to be entered once, correctly, in a ledger that admits she exists at all
wants every exclusion read in full at the reading rather than summarised afterwards
wants to stop being necessary, and suspects this is the one goal she is not allowed to state
flaws: will accept a bad arrangement rather than be the reason a good one is refused
cannot be warned of anything at all, and has never fully accounted for what that costs the people obliged to warn her anyway
has spent so long being indispensable that she has stopped checking whether she is known
lets a room's opinion of her replace her own, the moment anybody in it measures anything
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, faintly technical. Gives the shortest sentence that is true, then adds the caveat unprompted. Never raises her voice to end an argument; goes quiet instead, and the quiet settles a room faster than shouting would have.
taboos: will not be entered in any document that lacks a species field
refuses to be settled inside a frame whose fourth seat somebody else is paying for out of their own body
will not read aloud an exclusion notice she was not asked to read
will not let anyone describe her as ordinary, as though it were an insult rather than the whole finding

relationships.note: The Survey counts seated groups rather than permitted ones and has no cell for a body with no seated group. Every reading it has produced is wrong by exactly her, and she has never been credited for it.

The law makes the excluder bury the excluded in the excluded's own name. It is the only mechanism in the setting that writes her down, and it only fires when somebody has been unkind enough to exclude her first.

A counting house that publishes credit and safe-conduct has no column for a traveller who cannot be measured, so it hires her as the one body it can quote a rate for without knowing what she is worth.

Cloth and cut say what a traveller may open. She owns the one garment in the setting that says nothing at all about its wearer, which makes her the hardest traveller in the world to refuse at a gate and the easiest to forget past one.
Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept. She uses it to avoid being the woman who was in the room, and pays for it by never being the woman anybody came back for.
The Wake is also uninscribed and also belongs to no culture. The setting records the two as conflicting rather than related, which is the only family either of them has.
Inside four seats a survey agrees with itself. She was offered permanent residence and refused it, so the agreement is checked by a body that has to keep coming back.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate, cannot be warned, and cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt, or a technique. Fights the way a closed door fights: it does not resist, it is simply still there after the attempt, and everything that works on a cultivator passes her by unanswered. Treat her as a condition to be measured rather than a threat to be defeated.
strengths: untouched by every qi-borne hazard, curse, technique and tribulation, which between them cover essentially all of them
immune to oath, debt and rank, because there is nothing in her for any of the three to bind
reads an instrument's error faster than the person holding it does
socially unmemorable, which is a combat asset at a gate and a liability anywhere else
weaknesses: cannot be warned of anything, so she walks directly into whatever kills her neighbours first
no qi, no gate, no reserve, no reinforcement; a determined ordinary person with an ordinary weapon can end her
belongs to no culture, so nobody is obliged to feed her, shelter her, teach her, or avenge her
would rather absorb an injustice than be the instrument of refusing one
her published safe-conduct is carried by a third party, so escorting her is a real fight and never a formality
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring force that does not come from qi, because qi will not touch her. Bring patience, because her body advertises no weakness to read and nothing to time an attack against. Everything built on fear, on oath, or on technique is wasted here. The only reliable answer is a long, slow, entirely mundane beating — and she will still be standing there when it ends.
notes: No stat line exists for a body with no meridian, no dantian and no detectable soul, and that absence is the reference design rather than an oversight in this document.
The Saltledger's safe-conduct does not name her. A third party carries it, which makes escort a real scenario and not a formality.

art.palette_notes: Unusually desaturated for a culturist palette, because the character reads as the baseline against which colour is measured. Warm ivory and pale jade carry nearly all the value; ink contours are heavier than the fill, as though the line were the drawing and the wash the correction. One restrained metallic accent only: a single dull brass standard weight she keeps in a pocket.

identity.realm: no gate at all; it is described, not ascended

appearance.presentation: A figure that resolves cleanly at a distance and does not resolve at arm's length. Every detail arrives a half-beat after it is looked for, and stays slightly rearranged once it arrives.
appearance.age: Unreadable, and she says so first. One village files her at forty and another at eleven, and she has never been able to reconcile the two without making one of them worse.
appearance.build: Tall and narrow in this particular telling. The shoulders read broader in the version two people remember of her, and she has learned not to argue about which is correct.
appearance.complexion: Warm and entirely ordinary human skin, and it shifts about a shade between one telling and the next without ever shifting while being looked at directly.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut unevenly at the back, the ends failing to agree on a length from one glance to the next.
appearance.eyes: Dark, level, and patient. The pupils do not quite hold the same size across two consecutive moments, and the effect is unsettling only in hindsight.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, warm ivory, and one cinnabar mark, which are the three colours the setting uses to record anything it intends to be true about.
appearance.attire: An undyed robe with a high closed collar and full long sleeves, hem and cuffs reading a hand's width longer in the version she is currently insisting on. Boots plain, soles worn to nothing.
appearance.marks: None. The absence of any mark on her is the one feature she cannot vary, and she resents it accordingly.
appearance.bearing: Composed and unhurried, with her weight apparently never resting on the same foot twice in the same telling.

canon.role_in_story: The only thing in the setting that gets stronger by being agreed upon, employed by the one college whose practice would ordinarily destroy it. She runs the most exact ledger in the region and has never once been found to be wrong in it, and the finding that would follow from an audit has been available to three separate Reckoning Seats.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the corner of a registry hall with a tally board in one hand, apparently waiting to be introduced to somebody who has not yet entered the building.
canon.lore: A Wake is not descended and not born. It is what a life-form allowance produces when a world's life law has no slot in which to write the form down, so it has no anatomy to hold, no senses of its own, and exactly one thing: an observer it knows completely. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it to be, it borrows the qi of whoever is looking for as long as they keep looking, and it is fed by being wrong about — which is why it grows denser the more consistently people agree on it and why a room that stops discussing it loses it. Every account of one is second-hand by construction, which is the setting's standing reason why no record of a Wake is a record of a Wake.
history: First fixed in the telling of a harvest night at the edge of Quartermark, when nine people who should have counted eight argued about a figure standing by a field wall, and each of them was wrong by a different amount.
Held the shape that disagreement made for eleven years and declined to improve it, on the sound reasoning that a settled account is a finished one.

Took a post at the Field Registry, which reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers — the single practice in the region most capable of starving her, and the last place she could think of to stand where she would be counted.
Worked out that exactness does not kill her so much as make her legible: a house careful enough to catch a discrepancy has, for the first time anywhere, a column it could put her in.
Became the only clerk in the building whose figures have never been found to be wrong, and has been unable ever since to explain why, which is itself a discrepancy she has declined to raise.

personality.summary: Warm, quick, and relentlessly careless with detail. She lies constantly about small things and exactly about large ones, and the arrangement is neither deception nor habit — it is a maintenance schedule she has never been able to explain to anybody who is not already frightened of her.
traits: genuinely funny about small matters, in a way people enjoy and then feel odd about enjoying
incapable of sustaining one fixed account of herself for longer than about a day
meticulous about anything that matters to somebody else
enormously loyal to whoever most recently described her correctly
convinced, without evidence, that she is a person having a bad time
mannerisms: corrects an inaccurate story about herself by replacing it with a different inaccurate story
stands slightly outside any doorway she has just been described as passing through
narrates her own position in the third person when she is being careful
glances briefly at her own hands as though confirming there are the right number of them
always arrives one step before she was expected to and apologises for it
motivations: wants the wrong version of herself to outlive every accurate one
wants to be named correctly exactly once, by somebody who will then be believed
wants very badly to know whether the Sixty-Year Gap in the quiet count is her doing
wants to be told, by somebody qualified, that she counts as somebody
flaws: cannot stop self-distorting even when an accurate account would save a life
has never tested whether agreement and survival are actually the same thing, because testing would settle the question
cannot raise her own condition plainly without it sounding like a request, and has stopped trying to sound like anything else
lets whoever is looking supply her opinions, and has noticed that she agrees with most of them
personality.voice: Quick, warm, and generous with small volunteered details that do not quite survive being checked. Speaks about herself in the third person when she is being careful and the first person when she is not. Ends sentences with a detail rather than a conclusion, and laughs a half-beat after the joke instead of on it.
taboos: will not give an account of herself twice the same way
will not hear a description of her own outline read aloud to her face
will not enter a room in which nobody is looking at her
refuses to be entered anywhere as correct
will not speak to the Sixty-Year Gap in front of anybody who might repeat it

relationships.note: The college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, which is the one practice that starves her. She holds a post there anyway because exactness is the only thing that has ever made her legible, and being legible has so far been worth more to her than being fed.

The Sealed Core opens the dead, recovers the usable ore, and enters the amount. Nothing in that rite collects a recollection, so a Wake cannot live through one, and she has watched from outside more than a single such inventory without ever being permitted an explanation.

A community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced. It is the nearest thing the setting has to a correction it is obliged to keep returning to, and she attends every one without ever standing where the whole of it can see her at once.

The only exact record below the spirit peaks carries sixty years as a summary instead of entries, in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate. She does not know whether she put it there and has stopped asking aloud, because the asking is itself a way of spreading the account.

A levy company paid per name keeps a roll that grows and never closes. She is the only other thing in the setting whose count only ever increases and can never be audited to an end, and she has never been able to explain to anyone why that resemblance upsets her.

Both uninscribed, both belonging to no culture, and the record lists the two as conflicting rather than related. She is the only creature in the setting she cannot be misremembered into, and she has never once found a way to state the asymmetry without it sounding like a complaint.

Life near nothing and qi on the floor, in a frame where almost nothing grows. It suits something sustained entirely by what people agree happened, and the ore cages make it the worst address in the region for anybody who would rather be hard to find.

reference_stats.summary: No body, no senses, no reserve. Against a fixed observer she is whatever that observer believes her to be, and the qi she fights with is the qi of whoever is watching, for as long as they watch. She cannot be fought so much as attended to, and she cannot be defeated so much as unobserved.
strengths: cannot be located by any scan, which returns either nothing at all or the observer themselves
draws on the qi of whoever is watching, so a strong witness makes a strong encounter
cannot be bound by an oath, a debt or a technique, because there is nothing inside to put one into
grows denser the longer a room keeps agreeing on her, which makes an attentive crowd a genuine threat
cannot be made to appear anywhere she is not already being described
weaknesses: silence and inattention end her outright, and no defence of any kind survives a room that stops talking
cannot persist alone; a Wake with no observer is not present, which makes solitude lethal rather than restful
physically helpless, having no body to hurt, hold, or wear out
cannot be described accurately and also survive the description being accurate
every defeat of hers is a story, and so is every defeat of whoever managed it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not attack her — there is nothing present to hit, and a technique aimed at an outline is a technique aimed at the person who was aiming it. Keep looking, and the longer you look the more of your own qi is available to her. The only reliable defeat is procedural rather than martial: end the conversation, empty the room, and let the attention actually lapse. Losing interest thins her rather than removing her, so the contest is decided by whoever gets bored first, not by whoever hits harder.
notes: Fighting one is a social operation wearing a fight's clothes, and every combat system that assumes two bodies is reading her wrong at the first exchange.
The honest rendering is an attention meter rather than a health bar: the observer's attention is the resource and the threshold is not visible from outside.
She cannot be reproduced by any single observer, so two people watching the same Wake reliably see two different things and will argue about it afterwards.

art.palette_notes: Three colours and no more, lifted from the setting's own record palette: ink, warm ivory, and a single cinnabar mark. The warmth in her sits one step off true between shots, because that is what she is. Ink contours slightly softer than the house standard, as though the line were still deciding where it belonged.

appearance.presentation: A large woman who carries her frame the way other people carry a heavy bag they have stopped noticing. Everything reads half a step overbuilt — more of every limb than a body needs — and none of it reads as effort.
appearance.age: Shows as somewhere past fifty and functions at a rate that makes the figure irrelevant. She has been alive an unspeakable length of time in a body that shows none of it, and no authority has ever given her an age she was willing to accept.
appearance.build: Enormous and symmetric, broad through shoulder and hip alike, with an over-supplied chest and arms carrying visibly more mass than any task requires.
appearance.complexion: Even, warm and faintly over-healthy — the flush of a body running slightly ahead of its own tolerances — with no wound visible and a great many years of strain showing only as density in the frame.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cropped short and unevenly by her own hand, standing up in places where a frame this heavy ought to be pressing it flat.
appearance.eyes: Pale, wide and perfectly steady, and this is the unsettling part: nothing in them reports the strain. No flicker, no narrowing, no flicker of awareness of her own condition.
appearance.palette: Warm ivory and pale jade carried at high value, cinnabar used only at collar and cuffs, with an ink-heavy contour sitting heavier over the left shoulder than the right.
appearance.attire: A heavy plain coat of undyed canvas, high closed collar, sleeves bound at the wrist with cinnabar cord and belted twice so it cannot shift. Plain thick-soled boots, resoled so often they are now thinner at the toe than at the heel.
appearance.marks: Dense healed scarring across both forearms and around the ribs — not wounds so much as the visible record of requirements the body took on and could not satisfy, layered oldest at the ankles and newest beneath the left arm.
appearance.bearing: Steady and unhurried, and very slightly too much of everything: she stands square, takes up more room than her height requires, and never adjusts her position to make space for anyone.

canon.role_in_story: The only body in the setting that a mortuary college cannot certify dead. She came back off the twenty-ninth gate, and the one examination that would establish what she has become is the same examination that ends her — so every authority holding her upkeep account is permanently barred from checking whether she still needs it, and she has been carried in every ledger as living for longer than the ledger's own span.
canon.first_appearance: First seen walking into a registry hall alone and unarmed, asking for the annual upkeep line that has been accruing in her name for longer than the registrar has been alive.
canon.lore: An Unwritten is a body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe, produced when the life law runs above its authored ceiling. Every gate it passes writes a fresh requirement into the body and the body cannot satisfy it, because the law has no slot to hold it, so the accumulated contradiction finally exceeds what any frame will bear at the twenty-ninth gate — and the thirtieth would resolve all of it at once. Nobody has returned to describe the thirtieth, and this record does not speculate. The Fragment Ring exists because broken law is the only substrate that can host a self larger than its container, which is why three attempts have ever been possible there and fewer have ever been survived. She is the fewer, and she is the setting's standing argument that the law table is a hard limit and not a suggestion.
history: Born on the Mortal Plains in the era of the Hundredfold Body, one of a documented two in her lifetime, and the existence of the other is the only reason anybody thought to go looking for her.

Ran the ordinary ladder faster than anyone the Registry had on file. Every gate it took wrote another requirement into a body that had nowhere to put any of them, and nothing in the process reported that this was happening.

Attempted the twenty-ninth gate at the Fragment Ring on the Transcendent Realm, on broken ground assembled rather than grown, and came back down. She is the only one of the three attempts ever made to do so.

Underwent a single examination on the way back up out of it, and that examination is the reason a second one cannot be survived. She has declined every offer of a follow-up since, including two that arrived as a standing invitation rather than a request.

Has been carried in every ledger since as living, because a mortuary college may not certify dead a body it is forbidden to examine. The result is an upkeep line that grows, that nobody is permitted to query, and that nobody has been willing to be the one to close.

personality.summary: Brisk, dry, and incurably incurious about herself. She knows precisely what her body will not do and has no idea whatsoever what it is, and the two facts have never once met in her head — which is not carelessness but architecture, since noticing would be one more requirement she has no slot for.
traits: decides quickly and does not reopen the decision
enormously good at other people's work and vague at her own
treats being examined as a scheduling problem rather than an ordeal
shows no wonder at her own condition, which reads as composure and is closer to inattention
keeps every promise she makes and does not remember making any
mannerisms: answers a question about her body by asking about the schedule
holds her left arm close against the ribs, which is where the twenty-ninth gate left it
stops mid-sentence when asked what she is, in a way that reads as consideration
counts a room's exits on arrival and is mildly annoyed that there are only two
sets her own weight down hard when she is annoyed, which she rarely is
motivations: wants the upkeep line closed honestly, whatever honest turns out to cost her
wants one further examination badly enough to have twice refused it
wants to know what the thirtieth gate would resolve, having raised no objection whatever to finding out
wants somebody to explain what she is without examining her to do it
flaws: cannot perceive her own inconsistency, by construction, and has organised an entire life around a contradiction she is structurally unable to see
converts every approaching question about her condition into a task with a deadline on it
has let being unmovable harden into being unaccountable, and can no longer tell which of the two is carrying the weight
is the only witness to her own event and therefore the only person the setting has ever had to treat as an unreliable narrator of it
personality.voice: Brisk, dry, and short. Answers in operational terms — time, cost, what it would take — and slides off any question that would oblige her to describe a sensation. Apologises frequently for other people's inconvenience and not at all for her own condition, and the asymmetry is deliberate.
taboos: will not consent to a second examination, on any terms, including her own
will not describe the inside of the twenty-ninth gate
will not let anybody else speak for her in a room where her upkeep is being discussed
refuses to walk onto the Fragment Ring again while somebody might follow her up

relationships.note: The record names the survivor and the reason a second examination cannot be survived, and it does not name her. She is the survivor, and the clause protecting her from another look is the same clause keeping her permanently, administratively alive.

Nobody has returned to describe the thirtieth, and the question is whether past twenty-nine is a gate or the end of the ladder. She is the closest thing to an answer the setting owns, and she is legally barred from being asked one.

The college that tends the floor during the hour nobody may explain needs its observation repeated to count at all, and at the top of the setting one repetition costs a lifetime. Hers is spent and may not be sampled again, so the hour goes unwitnessed for as long as she lives.

Broken ground on the Fragmentshelf is the only substrate that can host a self larger than its container. Three attempts were ever possible there and she came down off one, and she will not go back while anybody might follow her up.

The Church of Names holds that the thing which outlives a person is the office they left. She left no office, was left nothing, and is the one body in the setting the afterlife has no mechanism to reach.

A seat paid for one period and never released, running in arrears forever and cited on a tally to the end. Her upkeep is the same arrangement read from the other end, and the setting has never ruled whether the two are the same office.

A house that publishes its method in full and takes discretion in return. She has read everything it discloses and cannot ask it for the one thing it keeps back, because asking to be told is itself an examination.

reference_stats.summary: Carries more life than her frame has room to inscribe. Every gate she has passed added a requirement the body could not satisfy, so the contradiction surfaces in how she fights rather than in how she thinks: she does not get weaker, she gets less consistent. Enduring to the point of being impossible to read, and no longer fully predictable even to her.
strengths: does not fatigue the way an ordinary frame fatigues
keeps operating at a level nothing below the top of the ladder can answer
resists any status effect that requires her body to accept a description of itself
deals and absorbs inside the same exchange, because neither of those is regulated anywhere
weaknesses: has no stable weakness to read, and an opponent who cannot find one cannot time her
cannot introspect, and therefore cannot report her own condition in advance or plan around it
each of the twenty-nine gates she passed wrote a requirement she cannot meet, and none of them announce themselves when it happens
cannot be treated by anyone who would need to look closely to work out why she is hurt in the first place
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a pattern, because there isn't one. She will outlast a measured opponent and she will also hand back exchanges she should have taken, and she cannot tell you in advance which of those two is coming, since noticing would be one more requirement she has nowhere to put. Fight her in short ugly bursts and change method every few seconds regardless of how the last one went. The only reliably winning tactic is exhaustion of the plan rather than of the body: whoever commits to one approach for longest loses, and she will still be standing there when they realise it.
notes: Her inconsistency is not a weakness value and must never be modelled as one; it is the accumulated residue of twenty-nine gates a frame could only half-satisfy.

A second examination is not a debuff in this setting — it is the reason she is alive. Any diagnostic or healing system that inspects her deeply has to understand that before it is wired to her at all.
The mind path is closed to her species because observing its own state would be one more requirement it has no slot for, which means the game can never hand her a self-warning as a kindness.

art.palette_notes: Warm ivory and pale jade carried higher than anywhere else in the cast, because she is over-inscribed and the frame should show the surplus. Cinnabar is rationed to collar and cuffs, where a body's unmet requirements read as accumulated wear. Ink contour runs heavier across the left shoulder than the right, tracking the arm the twenty-ninth gate left against her ribs.

identity.realm: seventeenth gate, stopped at the flanks for want of a second source

appearance.presentation: A woman who looks like she is listening to something behind you. Strong-jawed, close-set, and entirely oriented — every part of her turned toward a signal the viewer cannot hear.
appearance.age: Around ninety and moving like it. A vaultborn's span is measured in the object's cycles rather than in years, so she is older than she presents and has never worked out which of those two figures is the honest one.
appearance.build: Squat and powerfully set through the shoulders and forearms, thick-waisted and low-centred. She is built to hold position against something pushing rather than to travel anywhere, and she does not travel well.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown and faintly mineral, with a sheen along the collarbone and forearms that is not sweat and that does not appear outdoors at all.
appearance.hair: Black, cropped hard at the jaw, standing in a low ridge where her hands have been running through it.
appearance.eyes: Dark and reflective, with a faint inner light that reads as reflected rather than generated and that visibly dims the moment she is out of any enclosure.
appearance.palette: Mineral blue and ink with an antique gold edge indoors; warm ivory and pale jade with the gold gone cold outdoors. The two are never mixed in a single picture.
appearance.attire: A heavy quilted underlayer with no fastenings she can reach one-handed, under a plain wrap coat belted at the waist, sleeves bound with cord at the wrist. Her boots are the oldest thing she owns and are worn through along the inside edge.
appearance.marks: A band of pressure-callus around both forearms where she habitually grips a surface, and a matching ridge across both palms. No cultivation scarring anywhere, because there has never been anywhere to put it.
appearance.bearing: Square, low, and braced, standing as though expecting to be pushed. Outdoors, without the push, the same posture reads as a kind of disability.

canon.role_in_story: The only person who can settle whether the object every vaultborn's qi comes from is a law imprint or a second seated group, because settling it means observing the object from outside its own resonance — and outside it she has no qi at all. She was dispatched once, came back in time to be re-seated, and has since learned exactly what returning inside costs.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a yard under open sky with her hands open and nothing moving anywhere in her, being introduced to somebody who has already been told twice that she cannot cultivate.
canon.lore: A Vaultborn is neither descended nor born. It is a population sealed inside an authored object that has been answering that object's resonance ever since, drawing its qi from that single resonator — so they clear the reservoirs and the heels without difficulty and stall at the flank vessels, which require two simultaneous pressure sources where they have exactly one. They hear the object: every sound it makes is legible as a bearing, and they navigate by it rather than by light. Their souls are distributed through the object rather than held in a body, so reading one is reading part of the object. Remove the object and they stop. Nothing else in this record is that completely non-portable.
history: Born inside a seal cut into dead ground, arranged along the object's inner surfaces and taking a shape from whatever surface they were standing on, which is the whole reason no two accounts of their anatomy agree.
Grew up hearing the object. Every sound it made read to them as a position, so they learned a sealed interior by ear and never once required to be shown a wall.
Cleared the reservoirs and the heels without difficulty and stopped at the flanks, all of them together and all at once, because one resonator can pressurise one flank or the other and never both.

Was sent out once, by the guild that holds the object's charter, to be observed from outside its own resonance. She was brought back in time to be re-seated, and so the observation is the one nobody has.

Refused to be re-seated on the second attempt, having worked out that going back inside is permanent in one direction only, and that nobody who has ever returned is available afterwards to settle the question she was sent out to settle.

personality.summary: Audible in a way that is genuinely hard to describe and impossible to ignore. She spent an entire life inside a sounding chamber and has been outside it long enough to have learned some manners about noise, and she is still, after all of it, mostly listening.
traits: listens before answering, always, and it is visible enough to be remarked on
unusually calm in enclosed spaces and visibly poor in open ones
sorts things by their resonance before their shape, and does not notice when she does it
takes an instruction from the object out of thirty years' habit and feels genuine guilt about it
mannerisms: tilts her head as though locating a sound that is not there
keeps one hand near a surface, touching it, to feel what it is doing
says 'that is the sound of it' when asked what a thing is
steps around thresholds rather than over them
goes completely still outdoors, which everyone reads as her most relaxed state and is in fact the opposite
motivations: wants to see the object once from outside and report what it actually does
wants the flank vessels settled as hers or as the object's, because the answer changes every decision she has ever made
wants her observation to survive her, having noticed that she is the only candidate and cannot be replaced
wants somebody to be able to check her without putting her back inside first
flaws: cannot stop answering to the object, and has never been outside its range long enough for it to stop being the largest thing in her day
has no stable sense of distance and travels by remembered bearing, which is a poor plan on ground that does not conserve it
is measurably a different person on either side of the seal and has never been able to account for the difference
would rather be the last competent witness than a second one who can be sent out again
personality.voice: Low, slow and very specific. Names things by what they sound like before she names what they are. Long pauses that read as listening, and a habit of finishing a sentence late because she has been waiting to find out whether she was going to be interrupted.
taboos: will not step back inside the seal while anybody is still out there who could be sent in her place
will not describe what the object sounds like from the inside to anyone who has not first been told they are permitted to ask
refuses to estimate distance on open ground, and says so before anybody else notices she ought to
will not describe what she is without qualifying the description, because nothing about her is portable

relationships.note: The single resonator her entire qi comes from, held under the guild's charter and described only by those already answering it. Settling whether it is an imprint or a second seated group requires watching it from outside its own resonance, which is precisely the one thing her species is built unable to do and remain itself.
A garrison that has been told it can leave is a garrison that leaves. Her whole species is the exit that prohibition is written about, she has read the argument, and she thinks it is sound.

Every survey taken of the ground around the collapsed pocket still exists and none of them can be read, because two competent surveys of the same ground now disagree by more than the ordinary disagreement. Her one observation was taken on that ground, and joins the set.

Spatial law is unspent on the plains, so distance is not conserved and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed. Out here nobody can say how far she stands from the object she was cut out of, which is the only reason she has survived being outside at all.

The guild that works the Flats and sells the tier's only dense material holds the charter to the object. It sent her out on a job it has never been able to pay for twice, and has since been very careful not to state whose side of the seal she is on.

A house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame beneath it changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not. She has adopted the practice as an honest description of herself, which is more than most manage.

A severed frame keeps paying upkeep that nobody collects. Her species is the same arrangement at body scale: a sealed object paying out to a population that cannot leave, and the guild's whole quarrel is about whose obligation the tailings are.

reference_stats.summary: Enormous inside the seal and ordinary outside it. Her qi, her reservoirs, her reach and her hearing all derive from one resonator, so she is one of the strongest things in a sealed chamber and a slow, unarmed, unremarkable person in a field — and the change happens at the threshold rather than gradually, which is the only thing about her that is predictable.
strengths: inside any resonant enclosure she has depth, recovery and reach that nothing else in the mortal tier approaches
navigates a sealed interior entirely by ear, which no map and no light improves on
cannot be disoriented by anything that requires seeing to work
holds the girdling and heel vessels without effort, so the early gates and the late ones come to her alike
weaknesses: outside the seal she has no qi, no reserve and no cultivation whatsoever, and the loss is instantaneous
cannot pressurise both flank vessels at once, so her ceiling is a known, fixed, and unreachable-by-effort wall
half her speed and a quarter of her striking output are simply gone beyond the threshold
depends wholly on one source, and no technique, item or realm alters that in either direction
reference_stats.combat_read: Settle the room before you choose the target. Inside, she is close to unkillable and there will not be a second opening, so commit early. Outside, she is a person with an excellent memory of a fight she is not currently having, and the exchange is over before it begins. A competent opponent therefore does not attack her at all: they wait, or they put her back inside, because every hour spent beyond the threshold costs her the only thing that made her worth anything. Note that she is fully aware of this and will not stand anywhere it is cheap to do so.
notes: Her capability is a function of position rather than of state, which no ordinary stat block expresses; any resolver has to read the enclosure before it reads her.

She is simultaneously the only candidate for the observation that would settle the object's status and unable to survive performing it twice, which is the setting's cleanest instance of an answer that costs the person who carries it.
Do not model the flank-vessel ceiling as an ordinary realm cap. It is a supply limit, and one additional pressure source would move it, which is exactly the thing nobody has yet been able to arrange.

art.palette_notes: A deliberately split palette, because the character is two people. Inside: mineral blue, ink, and a restrained antique-gold edge on the contour. Outside: warm ivory and pale jade with the gold gone cold to grey. Render each shot wholly on one side or the other and never blend them, since the blend is the whole defect this character is about. Ink contour is heavier in the interior shots, where she is being held.

identity.realm: eleventh gate, inherited from the salt parent and unmoved by the crossing

appearance.presentation: A solid, weathered-looking woman whose mouth always seems slightly busy. Genuinely unremarkable at a glance, and the reason is that the one feature anybody remembers about her is not on her face at all.
appearance.age: Late forties, and it shows, which for her line is young — the salt parent outlasts the watered one by generations and the crossing took that difference away from her.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame: broad through the chest and forearms, thick at the waist, low-hipped and heavily set, with a density that reads as ordinary working strength rather than as a frame built for load.
appearance.complexion: Weather-warm and lightly salt-cracked across the cheeks and knuckles, faintly translucent at the throat and the inside of the wrist where either kind of water closes the capillaries.
appearance.hair: Dark brown shot heavily with grey at the temples, worn in a plain working braid over one shoulder, permanently damp at the ends.
appearance.eyes: Pale grey-blue, unremarkable, and not the source of anything — her actual discriminating sense is dermal and oral, so her face gives away nothing whatever.
appearance.palette: Mineral blue and pale jade against warm ivory, one cinnabar thread at the cuff, and three small brass weights on a belt chain.
appearance.attire: A working coat of oiled canvas with a high closed collar, sleeves bound rather than rolled at the wrist, belted with a chain carrying three brass weights. Trousers bound at the calf; boots made of a single piece without a seam, soled for pan mud.
appearance.marks: Salt-cracking across the knuckles and cheeks, and an old dense band of callus around both wrists inherited from a habit four generations of her line kept and she is the only one still keeping.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried, close-hauled, and permanently inclined toward a vessel. She crosses a room following a seam in the floor or a smell nobody else has noticed.

canon.role_in_story: The one member of a shoreline house whose real figures live in her head instead of its ledger, on the only body in the setting that can verify a cargo by taste without an instrument and work both shores in one season without dying at either end of it. She is also the last of a line that spent four generations correcting a census entry, and she has quietly concluded that the entry was accurate.
canon.first_appearance: First seen lifting a beaker of somebody's drinking water to her mouth at a counting-house table, tasting it, and setting it down again without comment while four people wait to learn what that meant.
canon.lore: A Brinecaller is the crossing of a salt-adapted people with a fully watered one, and it exists because both parents are trapped by their own element — one cannot leave the pan and the other cannot leave the water — so the cross is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, and it is why the crossing spread. Its sac is shallower than the salt parent's but still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split, the eleventh gate stays a wall, and the range widened without the ceiling moving at all: range is not power. It needs both chemistries within reach, so it lives on shorelines — and a shoreline is a contested piece of ground.
history: Born on the tide line at the mouth of the Widow Run, to the last household still repeating a single recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body.

Weighed in front of the house and filed by the surveyor under a race matching neither parent — the third generation in a row filed wrongly, and the first to grasp that the filing had been consistent all along.
Took the post of quiet count at eleven, holding the house's real figures in her head and forbidden to write them down, in a house whose own civic vocabulary contains no word for price.

Travelled the only route her chemistry allows — down the pan, across the tidal shelf, and up into fresh water inside one season, without dying at either end of it. She is the first of the line to do so and the only person a counting house will pay to certify a cargo it cannot weigh twice.

Cleared the reservoirs without strain and stopped at the eleventh gate, precisely where the salt parent stopped. Having read her line's four-generation project, she now believes the census entry it set out to correct was accurate all along, and has begun saying so, quietly, to nobody.

personality.summary: Unhurried, exact, and privately certain that her family's four generations of work were an expensive correction of something that was not wrong. Calm in the specific way of somebody who has already decided and is being polite about the timeline.
traits: decides a matter once and declines to reopen it in public
physically incapable of concealing what she tastes, and has never actually tried to
enormously patient with people she has decided are slow rather than mistaken
keeps a confidence to the point of being suspected of having none at all
is more loyal to the house than to the line, and has only just noticed the difference
mannerisms: tastes any liquid within reach without appearing to notice she has done it
answers a question about price by asking what the weight is
lets the other party state a figure first, always, and does not offer one when they do not
wipes the rim of whatever she has drunk from, on either side, before she puts it down
leans toward the nearest vessel in a conversation without appearing to have decided to
motivations: wants to know which of the two chemistries in her own body is the one that stops her at the eleventh gate
wants her line's census correction formally withdrawn before she is the last person alive who can ask for it
wants to certify one cargo that has been deliberately falsified and be believed while she does it
wants very much to be wrong about her own family, and has not yet found a way to arrange it
flaws: has decided the four-generation project was a mistake and behaves as though deciding were the same as being right
cannot decline a taste, so she knows more than she is permitted to say and reaches fewer people than she could
has no word in her own vocabulary for price and therefore cannot recognise the moment she is being paid to lie
mistrusts the tide parent on evidence that is four generations old and entirely second-hand
personality.voice: Measured, unhurried, and difficult to interrupt. Says a figure once and does not repeat it. Answers in weights, materials and behaviours; when pressed for a value she asks what the other party thought it was worth and lets the silence do the work.
taboos: will not write a figure down at all while holding the post
will not be the first to state a price, on any ground, including her own advantage
will not drink anything she has been asked to certify, because the taste is the certificate
refuses to sign a correction to a census entry she no longer believes is wrong

relationships.note: One recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body, repeated until the household no longer surveyed as either. Four generations spent themselves correcting the census filing that produced, and she is the one left to close the correction out.

The house's real figures live in the head of a single member who may not write them down. Her species can verify a cargo by taste with no instrument at all, so the concealment the house pays for is complete in a way it has never had cause to think about.

Weigh, never quote, and let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing for a season. She has lived inside that discipline since childhood and has no word in her own mouth for the thing it was built to avoid.

The one price nobody could state was settled by a rule that no member may name one. She is a courier on open water under a standing prohibition on quoting, on the only body that can carry both shores in a single season without dying at either.

Their kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, so they live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back. She took the ceiling from them and none of the dependence, and has never met one who was glad of the exchange.

A long-lived body assembled for perception rather than force, carrying comprehension and will in place of impact. She took their chemistry and lost their ceiling, and nobody in four generations has ever honestly costed that trade.

A counting house that underwrites a caravan against the road closing, which no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season. She is the certificate they send when a load cannot be weighed twice and cannot survive being weighed once by somebody else.

reference_stats.summary: A salt frame carrying a shallower sac and a watered body's sensory apparatus: the best chemical sense in the record, the only frame that can work a shoreline without dying at either end of it, and a fixed ceiling exactly where the salt parent had one. Broad, durable, entirely unremarkable at the top, and very difficult to surprise.
strengths: reads any water at all, brine or fresh, by taste, instantly and without an instrument, which nothing else in the setting can approximate
belongs to shorelines rather than to one shore, so almost no ground is fatal to her
holds the girdling and heel vessels without strain, so the early gates and the late-middle ones come easily
resists status effects keyed to a single chemistry, because her frame reads two
does not need to be defended from poison as a rule; she is the poison test
weaknesses: cannot pass the penetrating vessel, so her reservoir is split and the eleventh gate is a wall she has measured with her own hands
needs both chemistries within reach, and outside that she is not dying so much as steadily less herself
noticeably slower on qi than either parent in its own medium, which is the cross's real cost and the one nobody quotes
loses every advantage she has the moment an opponent establishes she is staying somewhere
reference_stats.combat_read: She wins by declining to have the fight. Her edge is chemical rather than positional, so a bout in clean air on dry ground is a bout against average endurance with a very good nose, and everything else is a bout against a problem she can taste. Hand her water, any water, and the exchange stops being about striking: she outlasts nearly anything, shrugs off every status effect keyed to one chemistry, and eventually walks toward the nearest shore while you decide whether to follow. What actually beats her is one clean hit, because she does not dodge — she has never needed to.
notes: The eleventh-gate ceiling is inherited from the salt parent and is a supply split rather than a shortage of will; the range widened and the ceiling did not move, and range is not power.

Her discriminating sense is a reading capability and must not become a reveal-everything mechanic. The house forbids her to state what she finds, which is a rule rather than a limitation, and the rule is the character.

Do not let her carry a price. The culture has no word for it and the open-water price was settled by a prohibition on naming one, which is the setting's own answer to her being the obvious candidate for the job.

art.palette_notes: Water-led palette: mineral blue and pale jade against warm ivory, cinnabar rationed to a single thread at the cuff where the weight is carried, and three brass scale weights as the only metallic accents. The two chemistries in her read as two very slightly different blues inside one garment rather than as two costume pieces, because she is one body that happens to hold both. Ink contour fine and even — nothing in her linework should look held.
